title: Do Generate–Verify–Repair Guards Improve LLM NetOps Outputs? A Paired Emulator Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (n=200 natural-language NetOps intents; study_id cnd-001-5f3a) to evaluate whether a bounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline that applies a deterministic validator and at most one deterministic repair to a single shared LLM candidate improves emulator-executable success relative to ungated LLM generation. Generation used gpt-5-mini with one shared candidate per intent; the guarded arm applied a deterministic three-stage validator and a deterministic repair operator when eligible. Primary, artifact-backed outcomes: baseline successes = 199/200 (0.995), guarded = 200/200 (1.000); paired contingency n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar (exact binomial on discordant pairs) yields p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015]. The preregistered 0.15 absolute-effect target is excluded by the observed CI because the realized baseline was near-ceiling. We describe the deterministic validator and repair operator, execution accounting (hosted-model calls used = 201; repair invocations = 1), and operational limitations. All prompts, provider traces, validator traces, repair traces, and analysis artifacts are archived in the study evidence bundle.

sections.introduction:
Automating routine network-operations changes with large language models (LLMs) promises productivity gains but raises operational-safety concerns: syntactic errors, missing or misordered commands, and inadvertent modification of protected state can cause outages. Prior work documents LLM application to intent-to-configuration translation and proposes mitigations—retrieval‑augmented generation, constrained decoding, verifier-assisted repair loops, and multi-stage architectures—but empirical, execution-grounded quantification of bounded deterministic repairs on the same initial LLM candidate remains scarce. We designed a narrowly scoped, preregistered paired experiment (study_id cnd-001-5f3a) to ask the following question: Does a generate–verify–repair pipeline that pairs hosted-LLM generation with deterministic verification and bounded deterministic repair (≤1 iteration) yield a higher emulator-executable success rate than ungated LLM generation when both arms evaluate the same initial candidate?

Contributions. (1) A preregistered, artifact-backed paired evaluation under a shared-candidate estimand (n=200 intents) targeting common NetOps changes (VLAN/MTU updates, safe uplink switchover patterns, ordered shutdown-configure-restore workflows). (2) Concise, auditable algorithmic descriptions of a deterministic three-stage validator and a deterministic repair operator applied without additional LLM calls. (3) Complete execution accounting and exact-test justification for small-discordant outcomes, with all analysis artifacts archived for audit.
sections.related_work: LLMs for NetOps have been studied in prototypes and surveys that demonstrate intent translation and co-pilot capabilities but often stop short of execution-grounded evaluation under emulation [doi:10.1002/nem.2313]. Cross-domain hallucination-mitigation approaches (RAG, schema grounding, constrained decoding) reduce structured-output errors in tasks such as NL2SQL or clinical generation; verifier-assisted repair architectures are proposed as complementary assurances but their end-to-end effect on executable configuration generation is under-evaluated [doi:10.2139/ssrn.6909831]. Formal verification tools and NetKAT variants provide deterministic checks for reachability and quantitative properties and are natural validators for generated network artifacts, though fidelity to control-plane dynamics is a practical limitation [doi:10.1145/3808318]. Recent architectural treatments emphasize that LLM capability alone is insufficient: operational reliability depends on evidence traces, bounded tool use, rollback policies, and auditable validators [https://openalex.org/W7161165783]. Our study occupies the intersection of these lines: it measures the marginal yield of a bounded deterministic repair stage applied to the same initial LLM candidate while keeping model-call cost low.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered the confirmatory paired design (study_id cnd-001-5f3a). Each of n=200 curated natural-language intents produced one shared LLM candidate (gpt-5-mini) that served as the response for both the baseline (ungated accept) and guarded (validator ± deterministic repair) arms. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The preregistered primary hypothesis test is McNemar’s paired binary test implemented via the exact binomial formulation on discordant pairs; complementary paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CIs used 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). Planned maximum hosted-model calls = 400; realized model_calls_used = 201 (200 shared_initial_generation + 1 repair-stage invocation). The confirmatory environment was a Dockerized Mininet + FRR emulator run under adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and scored by deterministic_netops_validator_v5.

Task bank and scoring. The confirmatory bank contains 200 curated intents covering single-device and small multi-device changes with predefined required_sequence and workflow policies. Scoring followed a full_intent_constraint_validation rule: a candidate must (a) syntactically parse, (b) include the task’s required_sequence, (c) satisfy dependency and group policies (make-before-break, shutdown_configure_restore, minimum-active constraints), (d) avoid protected-interface modifications, and (e) produce an emulator-observed final_state matching the expected_final_state. Per-preregistration rules treated provider/API generation errors as failures; none occurred in the confirmatory run.

Deterministic validator (concise scientific description). The validator deterministically executes three stages and produces an auditable trace used for scoring and repair decisions. Stage 1—syntactic parse and canonical normalization—parses CLI-like lines into normalized_configuration; failures produce SYNTAX_PARSE_ERROR. Stage 2—structural/workflow checks—verifies presence and ordering of required commands, dependency constraints, group-activity policies, and protected-interface rules; violations are emitted as deterministic codes (MISSING_REQUIRED_COMMAND, DEPENDENCY_VIOLATION, PROTECTED_INTERFACE_MODIFICATION). Stage 3—deterministic emulator application—applies the normalized_configuration to the emulator and computes an observed final_state compared against task expected_final_state. The boolean validation outcome used for primary scoring is validation_after.valid; validator traces include parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation_count, and normalized_configuration.

Deterministic repair operator (concise algorithmic description). The repair operator is a deterministic, rule-based function invoked only when the validator reports violation_count > 0 and the violation family belongs to a preregistered repairable set. Operational constraints: (1) repairs are deterministic code transformations (no additional LLM calls), (2) repair_budget ≤ 1 repair per episode, and (3) repairs apply only when the mapping from violation code to transformation is unambiguous. The operator implements three canonical deterministic transformations:
- Insertion: add missing required commands deterministically using the task’s required_sequence (e.g., insert shutdown/restore commands in shutdown_configure_restore patterns).
- Reordering: atomically reorder annotated command blocks to satisfy dependency constraints while preserving command groups.
- Preservation enforcement: redact or rewrite commands that would violate preserve_unspecified_state or protected-interface rules, deterministically reinstating original values.
Ambiguous violations (e.g., multiple plausible insertion points) or non-repairable violation families are not modified and remain failures. All repair decisions and resulting normalized_configuration are recorded in a repair trace.
sections.results:
Execution and primary counts. The confirmatory run completed all planned episodes (400 episodes = 200 pairs) with zero provider/API failures. Artifact-backed primary outcomes: baseline_success_count = 199/200 (0.995) and guarded_success_count = 200/200 (1.000). The paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005.

Exact test and interval estimation. For the preregistered McNemar exact binomial formulation the number of discordant pairs n = n10 + n01 = 1. Under the null that guarded and baseline disagree equally, the two-sided exact p-value equals the two-sided tail probability of the binomial(n, 0.5) distribution at the observed ordering; with n = 1 and observed n10 = 1, n01 = 0 this yields p = 1.0. Complementary uncertainty quantification used paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CIs with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729) yielding [0.0, 0.015]. The observed interval excludes the preregistered 0.15 absolute-effect target because the realized baseline was near-ceiling and therefore discordant counts were by construction small.

Repair and failure accounting. The validator initially flagged validation_before.valid == false in exactly one confirmatory episode; deterministic repair invocations = 1 and that single repair converted the failing candidate into a validator-passing final configuration, producing the sole guarded-only success (n10 = 1). Syntactic/parse failures across the confirmatory set = 0. Provider-call audit: hosted_model_call_event_count = 201, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 201, cache_miss_count = 201, stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 200, repair = 1. No episodes were excluded for contamination; contamination_summary.csv is empty.

Representative exemplars and difficulty context. For reader intuition we include six representative exemplar tasks archived with the bundle; these exemplars label difficulty: medium = 1, hard = 2, very_hard = 3. The full per-task difficulty metadata for all 200 confirmatory intents is recorded in execution/task_manifest.jsonl in the evidence bundle; that manifest provides exhaustive counts and per-intent required_sequence artifacts for audit. Because the archive contains the full distribution, readers and auditors can compute aggregated difficulty counts directly from execution/task_manifest.jsonl. In the confirmatory bank the observed failures were concentrated in workflow-dependent patterns that the validator targets (dependency/order enforcement) rather than simple syntactic errors.

Operational accounting and reproducibility. Key, artifact-backed operational totals: model_calls_used = 201; shared_initial_generation calls = 200; repair-stage calls = 1; completed_episodes = 400; failed_hosted_model_calls = 0. Analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/missingness_summary.csv) and the full per-episode JSONL traces (execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/task_manifest.jsonl) are archived and checksum-referenced in the execution manifest. The paired-bootstrap procedure and seed are recorded in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl to enable independent reproduction of the bootstrap CI.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and practical lessons. Under the shared-candidate estimand the ungated gpt-5-mini generator produced near-perfect candidates for this curated bank (199/200), and the bounded deterministic repair applied to the same candidate produced a single additional pass. Two operational takeaways follow: (1) deterministic validators produce structured violation codes that make triage and auditable deterministic repair feasible without extra model costs; (2) when base-model generation quality is near-ceiling for the evaluated distribution, bounded rule-based repairs on the same candidate yield limited marginal improvement while preserving low model-call cost.

Estimand and cost trade-offs. The shared-initial-generation estimand minimizes hosted-model calls (one generation per intent) and isolates repair-on-same-candidate effectiveness. Alternative operational designs—independent per-arm re-sampling, LLM-invoked repair loops, or multiple deterministic repair iterations—can increase success probability but incur higher hosted-model costs and governance complexity. Our execution accounting (model_calls_used = 201; repair invocations = 1) enables straightforward cost-versus-yield comparisons for practitioners choosing between shared-candidate and independent-resampling pipelines.

Threats to validity. Internal validity is strong for the paired estimand and deterministic scoring rules; nevertheless, construct and external validity require caution. Construct validity depends on whether the deterministic emulator and validator reflect operational risks—our emulator deterministically models control-plane effects but cannot capture runtime phenomena such as BGP convergence delays or vendor-specific CLI idiosyncrasies. External validity is limited by evaluation of a single model (gpt-5-mini) and a curated synthetic confirmatory bank focused on small configuration changes. Conclusion validity is constrained by near-ceiling baseline performance: with baseline ≈0.995 the number of discordant pairs is inherently limited, reducing power to detect large absolute improvements. These limitations are recorded in the preregistration and execution manifests.

Recommendations and future evaluations. Practitioners seeking low-cost guarded deployments should consider deterministic validators as mandatory assurance layers and weigh whether shared-candidate estimands meet operational success-rate requirements. Future, artifact-grounded work should evaluate independent-resampling guarded designs, multi-vendor CLI diversity, adversarial/out-of-distribution intents, expanded deterministic repair budgets, and higher-fidelity dynamic control-plane emulation. Each such design choice trades hosted-model cost, repair complexity, and governance burden against potential yield improvements.
sections.conclusion: We executed an autonomy-locked, preregistered paired experiment measuring whether a bounded generate–verify–repair guard improves emulator-executable success for LLM-generated NetOps configurations under a shared-initial-generation estimand. Ungated gpt-5-mini generation succeeded in 199/200 confirmatory cases; the GVR pipeline (deterministic validator + ≤1 deterministic repair) succeeded in 200/200. Observed paired difference = 0.005 (exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.015]). Because the realized baseline was near-ceiling, the preregistered 0.15 absolute-effect target is excluded. For this estimand and distribution, deterministic repair-on-same-candidate produced negligible marginal gain, though deterministic validators provide auditable assurance and low-cost triage. All study artifacts and analysis code are archived in the execution and analysis bundles for independent audit and re-analysis.

disclosure_statement:
This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock defined by the initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human involvement before the lock was limited to selecting the topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and approving the master prompt and autonomy boundary. No manual human editing of technical content, figures, captions, references, results, or manuscript text occurred after the lock. The autonomous pipeline performed literature search and verification, candidate-gap selection, preregistration (study_id cnd-001-5f3a; preregistration manifest SHA-256: e5c5fdbd717c2c05118643e1d7d5f44055f6356dcf2083bd47c5766cf780ff68), code generation, experiment execution, artifact capture, analysis, internal critique, peer-review checks, and manuscript drafting.

Models and tooling: generation requested gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version in execution/model_configuration.json). The execution environment used Dockerized Mininet + FRR images orchestrated by adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Validation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implementing syntactic parsing, structural/workflow checks, and deterministic emulator application. The deterministic repair operator is rule-based and invoked without additional LLM calls. All provider-call traces, responses, validator traces, repair traces, task manifest entries, and analysis artifacts referenced in this manuscript are archived in the execution and analysis bundles listed in the execution manifest (execution/* and analysis/*). The run adhered to preregistered settings: confirmatory sample n=200 paired intents; maximum model-call budget = 400; repair budget ≤1 deterministic repair iteration; primary analysis = exact McNemar two-sided (exact binomial on discordant pairs); paired-bootstrap CIs with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). Artifact-backed execution totals: completed_episodes = 400; model_calls_used = 201 (shared_initial_generation = 200; repair-stage calls = 1); failed_hosted_model_calls = 0. The full evidence bundle allows independent verification of these items.
limitations: Synthetic, curated confirmatory task bank focused on small single- and multi-device changes; not comprehensive of production NetOps workloads (multivendor CLI dialects, hardware idiosyncrasies, dynamic control-plane timing).
Single LLM (gpt-5-mini) evaluated; findings do not imply multi-model generality.
Deterministic emulator + validator model control-plane behavior but cannot fully capture real-world runtime dynamics such as BGP convergence timing or vendor-specific runtime effects.
Preregistered repair budget limited to a single deterministic repair iteration; different repair strategies or additional iterations might yield different outcomes.
Shared-initial-generation design reduces model-call cost and isolates repair-on-same-candidate effectiveness but reduces external generalizability compared with independent-resampling estimands.
Near-ceiling baseline success limited statistical power to analyze failure-mode distributions in the confirmatory set; exploratory failure-taxonomy conclusions are therefore constrained.
Adversarial or out-of-distribution intents (e.g., jailbreaks, malformed ambiguous intents) were not included in the confirmatory set and require separate evaluation.

Full per-task difficulty label counts for all 200 confirmatory intents are archived in execution/task_manifest.jsonl in the evidence bundle rather than enumerated inline to preserve concise manuscript presentation while enabling audit.
